To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a 560 Kb critical region containing the gene MN1 that is responsible for craniofacial anomalies and intellectual disabilities in two families with 22q12 microdeletions.
we report on two families with craniofacian abnormalities and developmental delay and overlapping 22q11.2 microdeletions.

we have identified two unrelated patients with overlapping 22 q12 microdeletions, one of which contains the MN1 critical region and the other contains the NF2 critical region, and we have demonstrated the importance of MN1 in human clefting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the critical region in 22q12 that contains the MN 1 gene and its role in cranio-facial abnormalities.
the identification and characterization of a critical deletion region in 22q12 that contains the MN 1 gene, which is responsible for craniofacial anomalies and intellectual disability.
the identification and characterization of genes involved in the pathogenesis of cleft palate, and the clinical management of craniofacial anomalies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

MN1 is responsible for craniofacial anomalies in patients with overlapping 22 q12.1 deletions, and that NF2 is not involved in the craniofacial phenotype in patients with overlapping NF2-MN1 22q12 microdeletions.
the MN1 gene is the causative gene for cleft palate in the 22 q12 region, while NF2 may play an additional role in the pathogenesis of neurofibromatous tumour formation.
MN1 haploinsufficient mice and patients with 22q12 microdeletion encompassing the MN1 gene are at increased risk for developing cleft palate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MN1 is a candidate gene for cleft palate, and NF2 is a candidate gene in neurofibromatiosis 2.

MN1 haploinsufficient individuals have a high incidence of cleft lip and palate, as well as intellectual disability and craniofacial dysmorphology, and that the MN1 gene should be considered in the evaluation of individuals with these features.
MN1 haploinsufficient mice and patients with MN1 haploinfficiency have similar craniofacial phenotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MN1 gene should be considered in patients with craniofacially anomalies, intellectual disability, and cleft palate.
the identification of the MN1 critical region will enable the development of a molecular diagnostic assay that could be used for the prenatal and postnatal diagnosis of cleft palate.
